name: Redis
model: In-memory keys holding strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams; Redis 8 adds JSON, vector sets, search, time series
engine_note: Single-threaded command loop over an in-memory hash table; optional RDB snapshots and an append-only file (AOF) for persistence
consistency: Single commands are atomic; MULTI/EXEC and Lua scripts run a group of commands without interleaving but do not roll back. Replication is asynchronous, so acknowledged writes can be lost on failover; WAIT does not make it strongly consistent. Replica reads can be stale.

jepsen.finding: A network partition with Sentinel failover threw away 56% of acknowledged writes; this is how asynchronous replication with failover behaves, not a bug that was fixed.
Showed that the proposed Sentinel plus WAIT design still destroys acknowledged writes when an old primary is demoted; WAIT alone does not give strong consistency.
The experimental Raft module (not stock Redis) had 21 issues, including split-brain lost updates and total data loss on failover; all but one were fixed in development builds.

scaling: Bigger machine first; read replicas; Redis Cluster shards keys automatically over 16384 hash slots, but multi-key commands must stay in one slot.
licence: Tri-licence: RSALv2, SSPLv1 or AGPLv3 (your choice), from Redis 8.0

licence_events.event: Redis moves from BSD-3 to RSALv2/SSPLv1 dual licence (source-available) from 7.4 onward; 7.2 and earlier stay BSD-3
Redis 8 adds the OSI-approved AGPLv3 as a third licence option alongside RSALv2 and SSPLv1

version_note: Redis 8.0 GA was 2025-05-02; several 8.x lines are maintained in parallel (8.2 to 8.10).
reach: Reach for it when you need sub-millisecond counters, rate limits, sessions, queues or a cache in front of a slower database, and the data can be rebuilt.
avoid: Avoid when it would be the only copy of data you cannot lose, when the data is bigger than RAM, or when you need multi-key transactions with rollback.
escape: Postgres is too slow for per-request counters and caching at memory speed.
chat: Per-user rate-limit counters, session tokens, and a cache of recent chat messages.
notes: Licence: since Redis 8.0 the user picks RSALv2, SSPLv1 or AGPLv3; classed copyleft because AGPLv3 is an OSI licence option, but RSALv2/SSPLv1 are source-available. 7.4.x (released 2024-07-29) is RSALv2/SSPLv1 only. Redis docs: Redis Cluster 'will lose writes that were acknowledged by the system to the client' because of asynchronous replication. aphyr.com is blocked from this network (HTTP 451); 2013 post dates were read from Wayback Machine copies. ElastiCache and Memorystore offer Redis OSS 7.2 (last BSD release) and steer new clusters to Valkey; Azure Managed Redis is built on Redis Enterprise.
